title: Introduction to Database Systems
description: Starter practice for data models, ERDs, DDL, DML, and SQL.

questions.question: What is a central role of a DBMS?
options: Translate requests while managing access to structured data
questions.explanation: A DBMS mediates between users or applications and the database while managing structure and access.

questions.question: Which model shows implementation details such as table names, columns, and data types?
questions.explanation: The physical or internal model captures the implementation-level schema.

questions.question: In an ER diagram, what does cardinality describe?
questions.explanation: Cardinality expresses how many instances may or must participate on each side of a relationship.

questions.question: Which SQL category defines or changes tables and other schema objects?
questions.explanation: Data Definition Language includes operations such as CREATE, ALTER, and DROP.

questions.question: Which DML operation retrieves rows?
questions.explanation: SELECT reads data from one or more tables.

questions.question: Which clause restricts rows returned by a SELECT query?
questions.explanation: WHERE applies conditions that rows must satisfy.

questions.question: Which clause controls the ordering of a query result?
questions.explanation: ORDER BY sorts the result using one or more expressions.

questions.question: What kind of problem occurs when deleting one fact unintentionally deletes another needed fact?
questions.explanation: A deletion anomaly is an unintended loss caused by poorly organized data.
